newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA-FINMIN LAUNCHES REUTERS BALTIC NEWS.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA-FINMIN LAUNCHES REUTERS BALTIC NEWS.

text.p: Lithuania's Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta on Thursday helped launch Reuters Baltic News (RBN) in Lithuania, saying the timing of the start of the real time financial news service was appropriate.
"The timing of Reuters entry to Lithuania is good considering the events which are happening here," Shemeta told bankers, politicians and financiers at a launch ceremony.
Shemeta was referring to the accelerated privatisation process in Lithuania and increasing attention of international and other Baltic investors to the Baltic country.
RBN is a real time financial news service covering the Baltic countries' financial markets.
Seven journalists will cover the equity, capital and foreign exchange markets of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania.
The new service, produced in English, is the latest expansion to more than 50 national news services provided by Reuters around the world.
These services are an addition to Reuters traditional international news service which covers 160 countries with over 1,500 journalists.
The Reuters Baltic News service will cover all news that is important to the Baltics financial markets including politics, industry and trade relationships.
Reuters set up its first operations in the Baltics in 1994, opening offices in Tallinn and Riga, as part of the company's Nordic network. It opened its first office in Lithuania in 1995.
Reuters was first active in the Baltic states from the 1920s.
RBN was launched in Estonia on Tuesday this week and in Latvia on Wednesday.
